item.research_question: How does the power of atmospheric plasma spraying (APS) influence the microstructure, frictional wear resistance, and corrosion resistance of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy coatings?
item.material_system: AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy coatings (HEACs) on low carbon steel (45#) substrates
item.processing_route: Atmospheric plasma spraying (APS) using mechanically milled powders (15–50 μm) with four power levels (H1 < H2 < H3 < H4); H4 utilized the highest hydrogen-gas flow rate and power
item.test_conditions: Tribological tests: Si3N4 ball (5 mm), 5 N load, 1200 s sliding time; Corrosion tests: 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, room temperature, 240 h immersion, potentiodynamic polarization, EIS (100 kHz–10 MHz)
key_findings: Volume fractions of pores decreased from 4.31 ± 0.90% (H1) to 0.59 ± 0.12% (H4) as APS power increased.
The H4 coating achieved the lowest coefficient of friction (COF) of 0.38 ± 0.08, indicating the best wear resistance.
H4 coating exhibited the highest corrosion potential and lowest corrosion current density among all samples.
Impedance modulus |Z| at 0.1 Hz for H4 was ~1459 Ω·cm², significantly higher than H1 (~382 Ω·cm²).
The H4 coating thickness was 80 ± 8 μm, showing significantly higher deposition efficiency than H1 (56 ± 6 μm).
Oxygen content in wear trace regions (delamination, debris, etc.) for H4 ranged from 14.27 to 20.22 at. %.
The passive film on H4 contained bound water (H2O) at 532.5 eV, which helps assemble dissolving metal ions.
item.mechanism: Increased APS power enhances the melting rate and alloying process, reducing porosity and improving coating density. During wear, multi-component metal oxides form and flake off to create a lubricating layer that prevents severe adhesion wear. For corrosion, the dense microstructure and the presence of bound water in the passive film (composed of Cr/Fe oxides) enhance protection against pitting initiation by Cl− ions.
item.limitations: The text notes that excessive gas flow in intermediate power settings (H1-H3) caused rapid cooling, leading to uneven melting and high porosity; also, the H4 coating still exhibited some pitting corrosion at phase boundaries after 240 h immersion.
item.future_work: The authors state that by changing processing parameters, it is feasible to acquire an AlCoCrFeNi HEAC with both excellent wear resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance, implying further optimization of APS parameters is viable.
quotes: The frictional wear and corrosion resistance of the coating are simultaneously improved with an increase of the power of APS.
The denudation of multi-component metal oxides and the formation of the particle-like debris on the surface of the coatings can adequately grease the friction process.
The improved corrosion resistance was attributed to the appearance of bound water (H2O) in the passive film.

Processing: Atmospheric plasma spraying (APS) using mechanically milled powders (15–50 μm) with four power levels (H1 < H2 < H3 < H4); H4 utilized the highest hydrogen-gas flow rate and power. Test conditions: Tribological tests: Si3N4 ball (5 mm), 5 N load, 1200 s sliding time; Corrosion tests: 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, room temperature, 240 h immersion, potentiodynamic polarization, EIS (100 kHz–10 MHz). During wear, multi-component metal oxides form and flake off to create a lubricating layer that prevents severe adhesion wear. For corrosion, the dense microstructure and the presence of bound water in the passive film (composed of Cr/Fe oxides) enhance protection against pitting initiation by Cl− ions.. Future work: The authors state that by changing processing parameters, it is feasible to acquire an AlCoCrFeNi HEAC with both excellent wear resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance, implying further optimization of APS parameters is viable..
